# CHAPTER 1 POPULATION SENSITIVITY REPORT

**Document ID:** TDD-SENS-001
**Version:** 1.0.0
**Date:** 2026-11-16
**Author:** Agent 2 (world structure / level architecture)
**Status:** PROVISIONAL. Derived estimate, not a measurement.
**Companion artifact:** `Docs/evidence/agent2/CH01_population_sensitivity.json` (generated by `Tools/world/sensitivity.py`)

---

## 1. The question

The Technical Director asked how the Chapter 1 population estimate changes when

1. policy-default NPC counts are varied, and
2. crowd-concurrency assumptions are varied,

with source facts clearly separated from assumptions.

The short answer is uncomfortable and important: **the estimate is 75% assumption, rests on 12 uncaptured scenes, and two policy parameters control almost all of it.** Capturing 12 detail blocks would do more for confidence than any amount of policy refinement.

## 3. ASSUMPTIONS — what the policy invented

From `Tools/world/data/population_policy.json`. None of these has a register basis. None is measured.

| Assumption | Value | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `expected_npcs` for AMBIENT NPC SCENE | 2 | People depicted in the 12 uncaptured crowd scenes |
| `crowd_concurrency_ratio` for AMBIENT NPC SCENE | 0.75 | How many depicted people are simulated at once |
| Cost unit: CROWD | 1.0 | Relative cost per simulated crowd actor |
| Cost unit: NAMED | 4.0 | Relative cost of a full agent |
| Cost unit: SCRIPTED | 0.3 | Relative cost of a looped performer |
| Cost unit: BACKGROUND | 0.05 | Relative cost of an instanced actor |
| Access multiplier: PARTIALLY ENTERABLE | 0.6 | Cost reduction for restricted access |

Cost units are **relative budget arithmetic, not milliseconds.** No capture exists.

---

## 4. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING

Only **CROWD**-tier scenes have a per-NPC cost. `NAMED` and `SCRIPTED` are **flat per-scene** costs, so their NPC counts cannot move the total at all.

Chapter 1 composition:

| Tier | Scenes | Sensitive to NPC count? |
|---|---|---|
| CROWD | 14 | **yes** — 12 of them are policy defaults |
| SCRIPTED | 19 | no — flat 0.3 units each |
| NAMED | 1 | no — flat 4.0 units |
| NONE | 12 | no — zero cost |

So the entire estimate collapses onto **12 uncaptured ambient scenes and two parameters.** That is a much sharper statement than a range, and it points directly at the cheapest way to improve confidence: capture those 12 detail blocks.

This is verified, not asserted — the `expected_npcs_for_scripted` sweep returns an elasticity of exactly **0.00** across values 0, 1, 2 and 4.

---

## 5. SENSITIVITY RESULTS

Baseline: **36.58 cost units, 49 simulated NPCs.**

### 5.1 Crowd concurrency ratio

| Ratio | Cost | Δ vs baseline |
|---|---|---|
| 0.25 | 22.38 | −14.20 (−39%) |
| 0.50 | 23.38 | −13.20 (−36%) |
| **0.75 (baseline)** | **36.58** | **0.00** |
| 1.00 | 36.58 | 0.00 |

Elasticity **+0.85**. Halving concurrency from 0.75 to 0.375 would cut the estimate by roughly a third.

Note the plateau between 0.75 and 1.00. This is **physically correct, not a model defect**: with 2 depicted people, `ceil(2 × 0.75) = ceil(2 × 1.0) = 2`. You cannot simulate 2.25 actors. The sensitivity tool detects and reports these flat intervals explicitly rather than hiding them behind a single slope.

### 5.2 Policy-default NPC count

| NPCs | Cost | Δ vs baseline |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 25.38 | −11.20 (−31%) |
| **2 (baseline)** | **36.58** | **0.00** |
| 3 | 47.77 | +11.19 (+31%) |
| 4 | 47.77 | +11.19 (+31%) |
| 5 | 58.97 | +22.39 (+61%) |

Elasticity **+0.88**. This is the single most influential parameter in the model.

### 5.3 Scripted NPC count — deliberately inert

| NPCs | Cost |
|---|---|
| 0, 1, 2, 4 | 36.58 (all identical) |

Elasticity **0.00**. Swept on purpose to *demonstrate* the model's structure rather than to vary the result. If this ever becomes non-zero, the cost model has changed in a way that needs review.

### 5.4 Crowd cost unit

| Unit | Cost | Δ |
|---|---|---|
| 0.5 | 22.88 | −13.70 |
| **1.0 (baseline)** | **36.58** | 0.00 |
| 1.5 | 50.27 | +13.69 |
| 2.0 | 63.97 | +27.39 |

Elasticity **+1.20**. Pure assumption; no capture exists to calibrate it.

## 6. NAMED SCENARIOS

Coherent joint assumption sets rather than single-parameter sweeps.

| Scenario | NPCs | Ratio | Cost | Sim NPCs | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LOW-DENSITY | 1 | 0.50 | 23.38 | 35 | −36% |
| LOW-COUNT | 1 | 0.75 | 25.38 | 37 | −31% |
| **BASELINE** | 2 | 0.75 | **36.58** | **49** | **0%** |
| HIGH-COUNT | 3 | 0.75 | 47.77 | 61 | +31% |
| HIGH-DENSITY | 4 | 1.00 | 58.97 | 73 | +61% |

**Range: 23.38 to 58.97 cost units, a 2.5x spread.**

All scenarios remain within the 60-unit chapter ceiling, but HIGH-DENSITY leaves only **1.03 units of headroom**. The chapter ceiling is calibrated tightly enough that an incorrect policy assumption of the high-density kind would consume nearly all of it. That is worth knowing before any scene is built.

---

## 7. A CORRECTION MADE IN THIS PASS

The sensitivity work exposed a rounding defect in the budget model. It is recorded here because it changed the baseline.

**Defect:** `_estimate_crowd` used `round()`, which in Python applies banker's rounding. `round(1.5)` and `round(2.5)` both return **2**. Consequently a scene depicting two people and a scene depicting three people cost exactly the same, and the model silently flattened under variation. Rounding to nearest can also round a cost **downward**.

**Why that direction is unsafe:** a population budget that understates cost is worse than useless — it is precisely the error that produces a frame-rate failure nobody planned for.

**Fix:** round **upward** (`math.ceil`) on the stated principle that overestimating a budget costs margin, underestimating costs the project. Scenes remain individually small, so the aggregate bias is bounded and is visible in §5.

**Effect:** baseline moved from 35.58 → **36.58** cost units and 48 → **49** simulated NPCs. The HIGH-COUNT scenario, previously indistinguishable from BASELINE, now correctly shows +31%.

Plateaus that remain (§5.1, §5.2) are genuine integrality effects, are detected and reported by `detect_quantization()`, and are not the same class of bug.

---

## 8. What this report does NOT say

- It does not predict runtime cost. No simulation has run.
- It does not cover the 41 uncaptured location entries.
- It does not validate the cost units themselves — the elasticities are relative to units that have no measured basis.
- It does not extrapolate to Chapters 2–8. Their categories are not ingested, and per the directive they will not be inferred from Chapter 1.
- It does not make any archetype, location or story decision.

---

## 9. The highest-value next step

Not a policy refinement. **Capture the 12 ambient-scene detail blocks.**

Those 12 scenes carry most of the estimate, and converting them from `POLICY_DEFAULT` to `REGISTER_DATA` would replace the dominant assumption with a fact. Every other improvement in this report is second-order by comparison.
